results.query: Which diagram illustrates theoretical throat, effective throat, and actual throat?
results.answer: In Figure B25 (Weld Sizes, printed p. 123, PDF index 135) of AWS A3.0M/A3.0:2020, fillet weld throat dimensions are illustrated: theoretical throat is the distance from the beginning of the joint root perpendicular to the hypotenuse of the largest right triangle inscribed within the fillet weld cross section; effective throat is the minimum distance minus any convexity between the fillet weld face and the weld root; and actual throat is the shortest distance between the weld root and the face of a fillet weld.

results.query: Compare the historical process atomic hydrogen welding (AHW) with gas tungsten arc welding (GTAW).
results.answer: Per AWS A3.0M/A3.0:2020, atomic hydrogen welding (letter designation: AHW) is an obsolete process classified in Table A5 (p. 74) and Annex D Table D4, whose definition is retained in Clause 4 for historical interpretation. In contrast, gas tungsten arc welding (letter designation: GTAW) is an active standard arc welding process classified in Table A1 (p. 69), Clause 4 (p. 32), and Figure A4 (p. 78).

results.query: What is the preferred standard term for heliarc and which figure illustrates upslope and downslope intervals?
results.answer: Per Clause 4 (p. 32), heliarc is a nonstandard term that redirects to gas tungsten arc welding (GTAW). In Figure B53 (An Example of a Welding Cycle for Pulsed Welding, printed p. 157), the diagram illustrates an example of a welding cycle for pulsed welding. Its parameter traces plotted against time include: WELDING CURRENT, ARC VOLTAGE, WIRE FEED SPEED, TRAVEL SPEED, SHIELDING GAS FLOW. The upslope and downslope current intervals define transition timing: UPSLOPE TIME transitions current up to WELD TIME (comprising HIGH PULSE TIME and LOW PULSE TIME), while DOWNSLOPE TIME transitions current down toward crater fill and POSTFLOW TIME.
